title: Generalized Biomedicine Discovery
abstract: arXiv:2610.00120v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In real-world clinical practice, medical images face open-world shifts: (i) long-tailed rare diseases, (ii) subtle lesions dominated by normal anatomy, and (iii) hierarchical taxonomies. Yet most open-world paradigms assume flat, balanced label spaces, leaving these biomedical demands unresolved. We introduce Generalized Biomedicine Discovery (GBD) and a unified benchmark spanning long-tail, anomaly, and taxonomy-aware discovery. Our key insight is that dominant known patterns form a visual manifold that masks subtle novelty. translated_abstract: 在真实的临床实践中，医学图像面临开放世界的分布偏移：(i) 长尾分布的罕见疾病，(ii) 被正常解剖结构主导的细微病灶，以及 (iii) 层次化的分类体系。然而，大多数开放世界范式假设标签空间是平坦且均衡的，未能解决这些生物医学领域的需求。我们提出了广义生物医学发现（GBD），以及一个涵盖长尾发现、异常发现和层次分类感知发现的统一基准。我们的核心洞察是：占主导地位的已知模式会形成一个视觉流形，从而掩盖细微的新颖性。受专家诊断过程的启发，我们提出了SCAN（惊讶诱发的互补顺应，Surprise-evoked Complementary AccommodatioN），它遵循一种受认知启发的感知进程：通过预测性抑制过滤预期规范，触发惊讶诱发的显著性来突出意外的偏差，并执行互补顺应将这些偏移整合到全局表示中。大量实验表明，SCAN显著提升了……（原文截断）
tldr: 提出受认知启发的SCAN方法，通过“预测性抑制—惊讶诱发显著性—互补顺应”的感知进程，解决医学图像开放世界发现中长尾罕见疾病、细微病灶和层次分类体系的挑战，并构建了统一基准GBD。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SCAN, a cognition-inspired framework that follows a perceptual progression of predictive suppression, surprise-evoked salience, and complementary accommodation to tackle open-world biomedical discovery with long-tailed rare diseases, subtle lesions, and hierarchical taxonomies, together with a unified benchmark called GBD.
